artifact: Corpus-evidence review of the six proposed CAT quant subject aliases
method: Judged on what the questions CONTAIN — their source chapter and their text — not on name similarity. Sampled every row for the contested mapping, not a sample.
verdict: 5 of 6 confirmed. 1 REJECTED: 'Averages and Alligations' must NOT alias to 'Averages'.

aliases.subject: Interest
aliases.evidence: 192 rows, chapters 'Ch 7: Interest' / 'Simple Interest' / 'Compound Interest'; questions are pure SI/CI ('A sum of money at simple interest amounts to Rs 600 in 4 years...'). The target name is more precise than the source, not broader.

aliases.subject: Progressions
aliases.evidence: 168 rows, all 'Ch 2: Progressions', all Arun Sharma Quant; AP/GP, arithmetic and geometric means. Progressions is a subset of Sequences and Series, which is the standard CAT grouping.
aliases.warning: Do NOT extend this alias to the other two series labels. 'Series' (53, Tyra) is NUMBER-PATTERN REASONING ('7 13 78 83 415 — find b'), not algebraic series, and belongs with reasoning/DI, not quant. 'Summation of Series' (64, Hall & Knight, only 14 playable and OCR-damaged) is university algebra and is out of scope by the standing instruction to leave the university-maths books alone.

aliases.subject: Ratio, Proportion and Variation
aliases.evidence: 140 rows, all 'Ch 8: Ratio, Proportion and Variation'; questions are ratio and proportion (pupils 1:4, wine/water 2:1, price proportion).
aliases.note: The target name DROPS 'Variation'. The content fits, but direct/inverse variation items lose that word from their skill name. Cosmetic if display_label carries the fuller title.

aliases.subject: Averages and Alligations
aliases.evidence: All 40 rows come from chapter 'Ch 4: Alligations' — not one from an Averages chapter. Checked all 40, not a sample: 27 use mixture/alligation language (alcohol drawn out and replaced, alloys, wine/water), 11 are alligation set-ups in disguise (lions-and-hens heads/legs; travel partly on foot and partly by bicycle), and the only 2 that say 'average' are mixture problems asking for an average cost — which IS the alligation technique.
aliases.why_it_matters: 'Averages' already holds 197 genuine 'Ch 3: Averages' rows. Folding 40 mixture problems in would dilute a clean skill and make a learner's Averages mastery partly a measure of alligation, which is a different technique. A learner weak at mixtures would read as weak at averages, and the remediation served would be wrong.
aliases.recommendation: Keep 'Averages and Alligations' as its own skill, or create 'Mixtures and Alligations'. No mixtures skill exists anywhere in the taxonomy or corpus today — this is a gap, not a naming collision.

aliases.subject: Time, Speed and Distance
aliases.evidence: 195 rows, all 'Ch 10: Time, Speed and Distance'; relative speed, head starts, meeting points. Pure word-order variant.

aliases.subject: Time and Work
aliases.evidence: 191 rows, 'Ch 9: Time and Work' and 'Time and Work'; men-and-boys work rates, pipes and cisterns. Pure word-order variant. (Pipes/cisterns is sometimes split out elsewhere, but is universally taught under Time and Work.)

if_applied_as_proposed: 40 alligation questions would attach to the wrong skill; the other five mappings are safe.
